regexTester.title: Regex Tester
regexTester.introDesc: A regular expression is a "search rule" for text. Enter a rule to instantly see what matches. Click an example to get started:
regexTester.noMatchHint: No matches found. Check your pattern or test text
regexTester.cheatCharClass: Character set: a, b or c
regexTester.errorUnterminatedClass: Unclosed character class [ ], add a closing ]
regexTester.truncatedHint: Match limit reached, only the first 500 are shown
regexTester.explainCharClass: Character set, matches any one of them
regexTester.explainNegatedClass: Negated character set, matches any char not in it
regexTester.explainGroup: Capture group: saves the matched content as a group
regexTester.explainLookahead: Positive lookahead: must be followed by the given content
regexTester.explainNegativeLookahead: Negative lookahead: must NOT be followed by the given content
regexTester.explainLookbehind: Positive lookbehind: must be preceded by the given content
regexTester.explainNegativeLookbehind: Negative lookbehind: must NOT be preceded by the given content
regexTester.explainStar: Repeat the previous item 0 or more times
regexTester.explainLazyStar: Lazy: repeat 0 or more times, as few as possible
regexTester.explainPlus: Repeat the previous item 1 or more times
regexTester.explainLazyPlus: Lazy: repeat 1 or more times, as few as possible
regexTester.explainOptional: The previous item appears 0 or 1 time
regexTester.explainLazyOptional: Lazy: appears 0 or 1 time, as few as possible
regexTester.explainRepeatExact: Repeat the previous item exactly the given times
regexTester.explainRepeatRange: Repeat the previous item a range of times
regexTester.explainOr: Or: match either the left or the right side
